problems.title: When a company looks for this kind of engineering
problems.lead: The center of the work is a system that already runs. Evolving an MVP, including one built with an AI tool, is an entry situation. It is not the company's category.

scale.title: The system no longer matches the operation
scale.body: The first release became the real system. Failures, queues and rework show up when more customers or more data arrive.

integrations.title: The integration loses or repeats information
integrations.body: ERP, bank, old API or spreadsheet. The data does not arrive, arrives twice, or nobody knows which step stopped.

legacy.title: The old system blocks the change
legacy.body: The operation depends on a system that is hard to change. The replacement has to live with what already works.

genai.title: The MVP has to hold real use
genai.body: The product already opens, including when it was created with an AI tool. It now needs customers, real data, and an operation that cannot stop.

services.title: What FISAM TECH does
services.lead: Each area below names an operational problem. The service page says who it is for, what the analysis covers, and what the site can show today.

architecture.title: Software architecture and engineering
architecture.body: A structural decision for a system that already has users, data and a routine. What changes, what stays, and what another patch will not fix.

page.problem: The structure of the system no longer fits the operation. Each new change raises the chance of failure, and the team discusses symptoms instead of the decision that has to be made.
page.audience: Companies with a system in use, where the next change crosses teams, data, or a process that cannot stop.
page.deliver: A reading of the current structure, the risks, what is kept, and a sequence of next steps. It is not a closed project design and it is not a guarantee of results.
page.method: The work starts with the paid diagnosis. If there is a project, decisions are written down and the build follows parts the operation can follow.
page.evidence: No architecture metric is published. The cases page names SigaBR and 637 Tennis Club, without numbers. Bradesco, B3, Itaú, Banco Next, Capgemini Engineering and Gerdau are the founder's prior experience, not FISAM TECH clients.

backend.title: Backend development
backend.body: Services and APIs the operation uses every day. The focus is seeing failure early, receiving the data whole, and being able to follow the flow.

page.problem: The business rule lives in code that fails without a trace, or that nobody can change without fear of stopping the routine.
page.audience: Companies that need backend for a system that already has customers, an integration, or an internal routine.
page.deliver: The services, APIs and error handling agreed in scope. The site does not publish a technology list as if that were the service.
page.method: After the diagnosis, the scope is split. The build follows what was written down, with a way to see what changed.
page.evidence: No backend metric is published on this site. The founder's prior experience in distributed systems is kept apart from FISAM TECH contracts.

integrations.title: Systems integration
integrations.body: Connecting what the company already uses, with error handling and a point where you can see where the flow stopped.

page.problem: Two systems do not tell the same story. An order, a payment, stock or a record is lost, repeated, or stuck in a step nobody can see.
page.audience: Companies that already run on an ERP, a bank, an API or a spreadsheet and need the information to cross those systems.
page.deliver: A map of the flow, the failure points, and what will be connected. The versioned SigaBR text mentions an integration with DETRAN via RENAVAM and Banco Rendimento, without a metric and without an attached document.
page.method: The diagnosis looks at the real flow before the integration is written. If the problem does not justify a project, the opinion says so.
page.evidence: The name SigaBR is published as a client, with the integration named above. This repository has no source, date or measured result.

legacy.title: Application modernization
legacy.body: Changing an old system while the operation continues. The plan says what stays up and what changes at each step.

page.problem: The system that carries the routine is hard to change. Stopping to rewrite everything is not an option the operation will accept.
page.audience: Companies whose current system still runs the business and has to change without treating downtime as a detail.
page.deliver: A reading of what the system does today, what can change in stages, and what stays out. There is no promise of a migration without interruption.
page.method: The diagnosis separates what the operation cannot lose from what can be rewritten. A project, if there is one, follows that order.
page.evidence: There is no modernization case with a measured result on this site. The cases page says what is published and what is not.

genai.title: Evolution of MVPs and products created with AI
genai.body: When the first version has to become a customer system. A review of what exists, what is kept, and what has to be rebuilt.

page.problem: The MVP works in a demo, or it was generated with an AI tool, and it now has to hold customers, real data, and an operation that cannot stop.
page.audience: Companies in that situation. It is an entry scenario. FISAM TECH does not present itself as a firm that fixes AI-generated code.
page.deliver: A reading of what the system already does, of the risks in data, access, integration and operations, and of what would make sense to keep or rebuild. The opinion may be that there is no project.
page.method: The diagnosis session comes before any rewrite. There is no published standard timeline for turning an MVP into a production system.
page.evidence: There is no public case of MVP hardening in this repository. The published names are on the cases page, without metrics.

cookieBlocks.title: What is not a cookie
paragraphs: The notice choice is stored in localStorage, under fisam_cookie_consent. Region confirmation uses another localStorage key. Neither is a cookie.
Internal admin code uses the cookie fisam_admin_session. That area is not part of the visitor navigation, and the public notice does not cover it.

cookieBlocks.title: Third-party scripts
paragraphs: The site code has no advertising pixel, Google Analytics, Tag Manager, Meta pixel, Hotjar or Clarity.

At payment, checkout loads Stripe.js or the Mercado Pago SDK, depending on the currency. On the scheduling page with a valid token, an iframe opens Google Calendar. WhatsApp opens when the person clicks the link.

privacyBlocks.title: Who processes
paragraphs: FISAM TECH TECNOLOGIA LTDA, CNPJ 59.897.573/0001-02. Channel for data subject requests: contato@fisamtech.com. No data protection officer is named in this draft.

privacyBlocks.title: Data the site asks for
paragraphs: Qualification: name, email, company, role, challenge description, budget range, currency, country, language. The record goes to the leads table. Country may come from the COUNTRY cookie or from the chosen currency.
Ideas: name, email, phone, idea, problem and stage. The same kinds of data go to leads and to a WhatsApp message.

Payment: lead id, country, currency and language. Email and name follow if they were sent. Card data stays with Mercado Pago or Stripe. The payments table stores provider, transaction id, status, amount and currency.
Scheduling: a signed token, the lead id and the calendar address, in the bookings table. The page with a valid token embeds Google Calendar.

Report: category, narrative, approximate date and relation to the company. If the person identifies themselves, also name, email, phone and a consent record. The destination is the whistleblowing_reports table and an attempted email to contato@fisamtech.com.

Navigation: the hosting country header (x-vercel-ip-country or cf-ipcountry) suggests language and currency. The code reviewed does not store the IP address in its own table. If the database is configured, funnel events may go to the events table.

privacyBlocks.title: Why the flow uses this data
paragraphs: To answer the contact and prepare the diagnosis. To carry out the paid session and open scheduling after payment confirmation. To process the payment. To record the report. To remember language, currency and country.

privacyBlocks.title: Operators and transfers
paragraphs: Vercel hosts the site. It is a United States company. The code does not fix the project region.
The database is Supabase and/or Postgres, through DATABASE_URL. Supabase is a United States company. The project region is not in the code.
Resend sends email from contato@fisamtech.com. It is a United States company. Without the key configured, the email is not sent.
Stripe processes payments in currencies other than the real, when the flow reaches it. Mercado Pago processes the payment in reais. Mercado Pago is an Argentine company.
Google Calendar receives the appointment. WhatsApp, from Meta, opens the Brazilian header conversation and the message from the ideas page.
When the provider is foreign, the data may be processed outside Brazil. This draft does not choose the legal basis for that transfer.

privacyBlocks.title: Data subject rights
paragraphs: Brazil's LGPD gives the data subject, in general terms, confirmation and access, correction, anonymization, blocking or deletion, portability, information about sharing, and withdrawal of consent, within the limits of the law.
The channel for those requests is contato@fisamtech.com. Response time, retention and deletion are in the pending section. They are not in force here.

termsBlocks.title: What checkout sells
paragraphs: One technical diagnosis session. The price published on the site is R$ 4.990,00, charged in reais through Mercado Pago. Test amounts in other currencies are not a commercial price.

termsBlocks.title: What the session delivers
paragraphs: A reading of the situation sent on the form, the risks observed, and next steps. Filipe Godinho Gomes conducts the session. The opinion may be that there is no problem that justifies a project.
The session is not an implementation project, does not guarantee a business result, and does not include a defined refund. Refund and cancellation are pending.

termsBlocks.title: Payment and calendar
paragraphs: Checkout creates the charge at POST /api/checkout/create. The confirmation that opens the calendar comes from the Mercado Pago or Stripe webhook, when the status is approved.
The scheduling link carries a signed token. Without a valid token, the calendar page does not open the calendar. The email with the link is sent only if Resend is configured.

termsBlocks.title: What the site does not promise
paragraphs: There is no availability warranty, indemnity, or scope beyond the session described. The ideas page is not a partnership contract and not an engineering contract.
The public content describes what the company is in a position to show. Names from the founder's previous employment are not clients.

compliance.title: Compliance and integrity program
compliance.lead: Institutional text already published by FISAM TECH TECNOLOGIA LTDA: ethics, anti-corruption and a reporting channel. It is not an ISO certification, SOC 2, or an independent audit.
compliance.securityBody: The site uses Vercel, Supabase or Postgres, Resend, Mercado Pago, Stripe, Google Calendar and WhatsApp. A report goes to contato@fisamtech.com when sending is configured. A visitor does not create an account. This is not a certification and not a statement of full compliance.
compliance.responsibleBody: The program text names Filipe Godinho Gomes as managing partner and compliance officer, at {email}. That is not the appointment of a data protection officer.

code.title: Code of ethics and conduct
code.body: FISAM TECH states ethics, integrity, transparency, respect, responsibility, equal opportunity and a commitment to the law. The text asks for honesty with clients, suppliers and partners, compliance with applicable law, protection of confidential information, and a workplace without discrimination, harassment, intimidation, improper favor, corruption or fraud. A breach may lead to an administrative measure and, where it fits, notice to the authorities.

anticorruption.title: Anti-corruption and anti-bribery
anticorruption.body: The program forbids offering, promising, authorizing, requesting or accepting an improper advantage to influence a public or private decision. It cites Brazilian Law 12.846/2013. Commercial relationships should rest on technical merit and contractual transparency.

conflict.title: Conflict of interest
conflict.body: The program asks that a situation in which a personal, family or third-party interest could influence a company decision be declared to the compliance officer before the decision.

publicSector.title: Public sector and bids
publicSector.body: The program says bids and contracts with the public administration follow Brazilian Law 14.133/2021, and forbids collusion, fraud, an advantage to a public agent, and misuse of privileged information.

gifts.title: Gifts, travel and hospitality
gifts.body: The program allows a gift, hospitality or travel only when it is modest, occasional and without an expected return. It forbids cash and a benefit to a public agent meant to influence a decision.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.body: The program points personal-data handling to Brazilian Law 13.709/2018 and to the privacy page. The privacy page is a draft and lists what still depends on approval, including a data protection officer and a retention period.

channel.title: Reporting channel
channel.body: A form exists. With the option not to identify oneself left on, name, email and phone are not sent. The narrative may identify the person, and the submission passes through hosting and email. No investigation deadline is published. The company states that it does not tolerate retaliation for a good-faith report. That sentence is a commitment of the program, not a technical control of the site.

governance.title: Review
governance.body: The program says it will be reviewed when operations, the law or the corporate structure change. It is not an ISO certification, an external badge, or an independent audit.

whistleblowing.title: Reporting channel
whistleblowing.lead: A form that stores the report. Identification is optional. The page does not promise technical anonymity, an investigation deadline, or protection the system does not implement.
whistleblowing.scopeBody: Category, narrative, approximate date and relation to the company. The form categories are corruption or bribery, fraud, harassment, conflict of interest, another irregularity, and other.
whistleblowing.guaranteesBody: The option not to identify oneself starts checked. In that case the form does not send name, email or phone. If the person unchecks it and identifies themselves, those data are stored and consent becomes required. The text of the report may identify someone. Hosting and email are not an anonymity channel. The company states, in the compliance program, that it does not tolerate retaliation for a good-faith report. That is not a software control.
whistleblowing.howBody: If the database stores the report, the page shows a protocol in the form FT-WB, with the date and a suffix. If the record is not persisted, the page does not show a protocol. There is an attempt to email contato@fisamtech.com with the protocol and an excerpt of up to 280 characters. The email leaves only if Resend is configured.
whistleblowing.anonymous: I do not want to give my name, email or phone
whistleblowing.name: Name
whistleblowing.consent: I authorize storing my name, email and phone with this report.
whistleblowing.disclaimer: Do not include someone else's data without need. If you identify yourself, consent is required to send.
whistleblowing.error: The report could not be sent.
whistleblowing.degraded: The report was not stored. There is no protocol. Try again or write to contato@fisamtech.com.
whistleblowing.successBody: Keep the protocol. It confirms the database record, not an investigation deadline.
